definitions.gloss: to investigate thoroughly; to get to the bottom of
definitions.explanation: To pursue the truth or essence of something through deep study or inquiry. Emphasizes the intellectual process of thorough examination.

definitions.gloss: to master; to pursue to the utmost
definitions.explanation: To reach the highest level of skill or understanding in a field or discipline through dedicated practice and study.

examples.japanese: {原因|げんいん}を{究|きわ}めるために{調査|ちょうさ}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: We continued the investigation to get to the bottom of the cause.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{生涯|しょうがい}をかけて{学問|がくもん}を{究|きわ}めた{人|ひと}だ。
examples.english: He was someone who devoted his life to the pursuit of scholarship.
To master the art of tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: {武術|ぶじゅつ}を{究|きわ}めるには{長年|ながねん}の{修行|しゅぎょう}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Mastering martial arts requires years of training.

examples.japanese: {一|ひと}つの{道|みち}を{究|きわ}めることは{簡単|かんたん}ではないが、{大|おお}きな{喜|よろこ}びがある。
examples.english: Mastering a single discipline is not easy, but it brings great joy.

notes:
{究|きわ}める is a transitive ichidan verb.

ASPECT (ている):
{究|きわ}めている indicates an ongoing pursuit or a state of having mastered something.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [subject]を{究|きわ}める: to investigate / master something

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {真理|しんり}を{究|きわ}める: to pursue the truth
- {学問|がくもん}を{究|きわ}める: to pursue scholarship deeply
- {道|みち}を{究|きわ}める: to master a discipline

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {究|きわ}める: to investigate deeply or master (intellectual/spiritual pursuit)
- {極|きわ}める: to reach the extreme or pinnacle (emphasizes the peak or limit)
- {研究|けんきゅう}する: to research (academic, more neutral)
